curriculum.subject: English Language Activities
curriculum.outcomeText: position reading materials and sit appropriately while reading

interactions.prompt: Which child is ready to read?
choices: Sitting upright with the book open
Holding the book behind the head
interactions.answer: Sitting upright with the book open
interactions.feedback: Yes! Sitting upright helps us read comfortably.
interactions.retryHint: Choose the child whose back is up and whose book can be seen.

interactions.prompt: Where should an open book rest while you read?
interactions.feedback: Great! A desk or lap keeps the book steady.
interactions.retryHint: Pick a safe, steady place where both pages are easy to see.

interactions.prompt: Sort each reading habit into ready or not-ready.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap a habit, then tap ready or not-ready.
interactions.feedback: Well done! You found the habits that make reading easier.
interactions.retryHint: Ready habits keep your body comfortable and the words easy to see.

interactions.prompt: Amina's book is sideways. What should she do first?
interactions.feedback: Correct! Upright pages put words in the right position.
interactions.retryHint: Think about which way letters should face.

interactions.prompt: Match each reading problem to the helpful action.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap a problem, then tap the action that fixes it.
interactions.feedback: Excellent! Each action makes reading safer and clearer.
interactions.retryHint: Ask what would make the body comfortable and the page easy to see.

interactions.prompt: Show your best reading setup: feet steady, back upright, and what else?
choices: Book upright at a comfortable distance
interactions.answer: Book upright at a comfortable distance
interactions.feedback: Super! Your whole reading setup is ready.
interactions.retryHint: Choose the safe position that lets you see both page and words.
